svg.title: When to use an agentic loop and when not to
svg.desc: Two columns. Use loops when the next step depends on real feedback, success is checkable, and mistakes are cheap to undo. Skip loops for one-shot tasks, irreversible actions, and work that needs a known deterministic pipeline.
svg.text: A simple rule for choosing a loop

g.text:  The next action depends on the last result
 Done can be checked by a script or test
 Mistakes are cheap to undo (git, sandbox)
 Work spans files, tools, or retries
 You can name a step cap and a budget
Examples
Bugfix with a failing test
Refactor + typecheck + lint
Migrate a module, keep tests green
Triage CI failures on a branch
 One LLM call already finishes the job
 Success is a matter of taste, not a check
 The action is irreversible or high-stakes
 You need a fixed, auditable pipeline
 Latency or cost budgets forbid retries
Examples
Rename a symbol you already know
Draft a design doc or commit message
Deploy, migrate data, send email
Change billing or auth in production
